doc.title: Eddie Miller and Pete Fountain Interview, 1970-01-09

chapter: Callers, Bourbon Street and big bands
title: An elderly caller invites herself to the club
summary: A 70-year-old woman who has never been in a nightclub chats with Pete, who invites her to hear the music.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Thanks for calling, Ted. 522-3791. We have three lines open. Give us a call. See what happens there. Go ahead, please. You're on the air.
I want to tell you I enjoy your time.
And each year I wait like cases on a monument when you come up to the stand there on Canal Street. I never see you in person. I'm a gentleman. I view you with the television.
I was born and raised in New Orleans 70 years ago. Never have seen the inside of a nightclub in my life.

Well, you're going to have to come to mine once. I think you'd enjoy it. I don't know how I get there. I'm a lady now, you know. Well, we'd see that you get there some kind of way. If you'll let us know, we sure would.
I don't know. Do you think I would be doing...
No, I think you'd enjoy it. Really? You could have a Coke or some coffee.
But I don't smoke or drink. I'd be a wet blanket.
No, I know. You could have a little Coke and enjoy it. You enjoy the jazz.
You enjoy the music. Good night.

Wonderful. I loved your band. And I was here at the record. I was at the children, you know. My husband died now three years ago. And I haven't danced since the day I married. He didn't like dancing. I loved it.
Well, everybody from New Orleans used to love to dance.
But I wasn't committed to go to Catholic affairs, to house parties and things of that sort. I was raped by straight Irish parents or Catholics, you know. We weren't allowed to mix too much.
See, my wife thinks I'm bad. Thank you, love.
